# Start / stop station -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** The operator contract, on its own. Start runs the belt, Stop stops it, and the mushroom latches a trip that only Reset clears. Feed a batch of the size the panel's pot asks for and stop when it is made.

**Done when.** The batch count reaches the setpoint and the line stops itself. Pressing Start while tripped does nothing; releasing the mushroom does not restart it either. Only Reset then Start brings it back.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`start_stop_station.st`](start_stop_station.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Start / stop station" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/start_stop_station.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   ```bash
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   (From a source checkout: `cd sidecar && python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`.
   If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add `-o host 0.0.0.0` and read the warning
   it prints.) Check the address map it prints against the table below.
3. Compile `start_stop_station.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh start_stop_station.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 6 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 7 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 4 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 2 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses -- and pass the port it prints:

   ```bash
   python tools/grade.py --scene start-stop-station
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `belt.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `BeltFault` %IX100.0 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn, whatever it is told |  |
| `belt.rotate` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `BeltRotate` %QX100.0 | run the belt | yes |
| `counter.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x0 + 3x1 | `CounterCountHi` %IW100 + `CounterCountLo` %IW101 -> `CounterCount` : DINT | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |
| `emitter.emit` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `EmitterEmit` %QX100.1 | rising edge = feed one carton; hold each level well over one poll | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.1 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.2 | green lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `PanelRed` %QX100.3 | red lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `PanelReset` %IX100.2 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x2 + 3x3 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW102 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW103 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 0..50 pcs (starts at 12) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `PanelStart` %IX100.3 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `PanelStop` %IX100.4 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `part_present.detect` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `PartPresentDetect` %IX100.5 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam | yes |
| `produced.value` | PLC writes | int | 4x0 + 4x1 | `ProducedValueHi` %QW100 + `ProducedValueLo` %QW101 -> `ProducedValue` : DINT | number shown on the display (pcs) | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `TowerGreen` %QX100.4 | tower lamp, green |  |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `TowerRed` %QX100.5 | tower lamp, red |  |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `TowerYellow` %QX100.6 | tower lamp, yellow |  |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 3:
  `counter.count`, `panel.setpoint`, `produced.value`. The program's first and
  last sections move them between the registers and plain DINT/REAL variables,
  so your logic never sees a register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the
  *number* (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the starter
  rebuilds a REAL bit by bit instead.
  [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh) compiles the helpers with
  OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
